anomalies.obs: On the Thermocouple sheet the shared SPI clock net NET0011 is the pin-5 (SCK) net of all three MAX31855s (U5/U7/U10), and the three chip-select nets are NET0015 (U10 pin6), NET0002 (U7 pin6) and NET0001 (U5 pin6). On the MCU sheet these same nets land on the wrong ESP32-C3 GPIOs: NET0011/SCK -> U4 pin18 = GPIO04; NET0015/CS -> pin19 = GPIO03; NET0002/CS -> pin20 = GPIO05; NET0001/CS -> pin21 = GPIO06; and pin22 = GPIO07 is left unconnected. Only SO (NET0016 -> pin16 = GPIO10) matches the spec.
anomalies.exp: The specification fixes the SPI/CS assignment: 'SPI2 on GPIO5/GPIO10, CS pins GPIO4/6/7' and 'tied to the ESP32 (U1 GPIO5/SCK, GPIO10/SO)' with 'separate nets CS0/CS1/CS2, driven by ESP32 GPIO4/GPIO6/GPIO7 respectively'. So SCK must be on GPIO5 and the three CS lines on GPIO4/6/7.

anomalies.impact: The firmware's SPI2 peripheral is configured on GPIO5 (SCK) and GPIO4/6/7 (CS), but the board routes SCK to GPIO4, a CS to GPIO3, a CS to GPIO5 and leaves GPIO7 (CS2) floating. The MCU would clock the bus on a CS pin and toggle CS on the SCK/USB pins, so none of the three thermocouple channels can be read correctly; all zones would report faults and the heater control loop would never see valid temperatures.

parsed.summary: The power, heater, USB-C and buck sections match the spec, but the thermocouple SPI bus is misrouted on the MCU: SCK is tied to GPIO4 (spec: GPIO5), the chip-selects to GPIO3/5/6 (spec: GPIO4/6/7), and GPIO7 is left unconnected, contradicting the firmware's fixed GPIO5/GPIO10 + GPIO4/6/7 assignment and breaking all three thermocouple reads.
